description.text:
Internal bridge between treeland and the user-session treeland-session-helper.
Treeland is a multi-user compositor and does not host per-user-session D-Bus
itself, so it asks treeland-session-helper, running in the user session, to
map a process (identified by a pidfd) to its application identifier and
sandbox engine name. treeland-session-helper answers over this Wayland
protocol; it in turn resolves the request through D-Bus with
dde-application-manager. This protocol is only for that dedicated
treeland-session-helper bridge, not a general application-developer API,
and regular clients must not bind it.

The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall",
"shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may",
and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as
described in RFC 2119.

Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.
description.summary: app id resolver bridge for treeland

description.text:
Factory global for creating resolver objects. Typically exactly one
treeland-session-helper instance (a Wayland client in the user
session) binds this interface and serves identification requests
coming from the compositor. Only the treeland-session-helper bridge
should bind this global; regular application clients must not use it.
description.summary: manager for the app id resolver bridge

description.text:
Destroy the manager object. Existing resolver objects remain
valid and must be destroyed independently.

Create a resolver object. Only one resolver may be registered
per session. Treeland is a multi-user compositor; different user
sessions may each register their own resolver. If a resolver is
already bound in the same session, the compositor will raise
the resolver_already_exists error and will not create a new
resolver object.

entries.name: resolver_already_exists
entries.summary: a resolver is already registered in this session

description.text:
Per-session resolver object created through the manager. The
compositor sends identify_request events carrying a pidfd, and
treeland-session-helper must respond exactly once per request via
the respond request. If resolution fails it responds with an empty
app_id.

Destroy the resolver object. The compositor will no longer send
identify_request events after this request is processed.

Respond to a prior identify_request event. treeland-session-helper
must call this exactly once for each identify_request. If the
application cannot be identified, respond with an empty app_id. The
sandbox_engine_name must always be provided and describes the
security context in which the process is running (container,
sandbox, etc.).

args.name: app_id
args.summary: the resolved application identifier, or empty string on failure

args.name: sandbox_engine_name
args.summary: the sandbox engine or security context name

description.text:
Sent by the compositor to ask treeland-session-helper to resolve
a process to an application identifier. The compositor emits this
event each time it needs to identify a process for which it does not
already have a cached result. treeland-session-helper must respond
exactly once via the respond request using the provided request_id.
Failure to respond in a timely manner may cause the compositor
to treat the process as unidentified.
